 ORDER Heard Sri B.Anwar Basha, learned counsel for the petitioner and Shri Praveena Y. Devareddiyavara,
learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.

2. The petitioner herein is accused No.1 in Crime No.06/2023 of Sirigiri Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(n), 498A, 504 of Indian Penal Code (for short "IPC") and Sections 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 of POCSO Act 2012, and Sections 9, 10 and 11 of Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, before the Additional District and Sessions Judge, F.T.S.C. I, Ballari.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, F.T.S.C. I, Ballari
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. The petitioner is the husband of the victim.
It is stated in the complaint that she married the petitioner on 30.05.2021.
Thereafter, she started residing with the petitioner and her in-laws at matrimonial house.

It is alleged in the complaint that during the said stay, her brother-in-law,
namely, Basavaraj one or the other pretext used to trouble her and tried to outrage her modesty by seeking sexual favour from the complainant.

It is further stated that the said Basavaraj tried to NC:
2023:KHC-D:13115 commit rape thrice during her stay.
However, she did not allow him to proceed further.
Such being the fact, the complainant became pregnant.
The petitioner and the complainant went to Ballari hospital for routine check-up and came back to the house.

Thereafter, the in-laws including the brother-in-law have instigated the petitioner to get the complainant for medical check-up and in the meantime, the in-laws have requested one of the staffs of the hospital to get her aborted.
Accordingly, when she went for check-up, an injection was administered.
Consequently, an abortion had taken place.
Thereafter, the complainant went to her parents' house and decided to lodge a complaint against the family members of her in-laws and against the petitioner.
It is stated that the petitioner was minor as on the date of marriage.

The jurisdictional police have registered a case against the petitioner and others for the offences punishable under provisions stated supra.
4.
It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is a legally wedded husband.
The actual age of the victim was not disclosed as on the date of marriage.
The petitioner under the impression that she has NC: 2023:KHC-D:13115 completed 18 years and married the victim as per the tradition and custom.
However, when the complainant became pregnant and went for medical check-up, it was diagnosed and identified that the complainant was minor.

Accordingly,
the alleged offences have been registered.
It is further submitted that the petitioner being the husband of the complainant, he was taking care of the victim with utmost integrity.

If the petitioner Somashekhara Alias P Somshekhar vs The State Of Karnataka on 9 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153750331/
2 is in judicial custody, the life of the complainant certainly would be miserable.

sentences.text: The entire allegations made in the complaint disclose about the brother-in-law, father-in-law and mother-in- law not against the petitioner.

The only offence which gets attracted against the petitioner is Sections 9, 10,
11 of the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006.
Though other offences are stated to be attracted against the petitioner, there is an exception to Section 375 IPC.
As per the said exception, the petitioner is exempted from being prosecuted for the above said offence.
5. It is further submitted that the petitioner is the resident of Gosbal village, Shiraguppa Taluk and he is a farmer and he has to look after his aged parents and also the complainant.
The petitioner will abide the conditions imposed NC: 2023:KHC-D:13115 by this Court in the event of his release on bail.
Making such submission, the learned counsel for the petitioner prays to allow the petition.
6. Per contra, the learned High Court Government Pleader orally objected the bail petition and submitted that the complainant is aged about 17 years and 9 months as on the date of the marriage.
The family members have performed the marriage knowingly that she is a minor.

Due to said marriage, she became pregnant and her pregnancy got aborted by the in- laws including the petitioner and there are allegations made against her brother-in-law regarding outraging her modesty.
There is likelihood of threat to her life, if the petitioner is enlarged on bail.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for bail.
Making such submission, the learned High Court Government Pleader prays to dismiss the petition.
7. Having heard learned counsel for respective parties and on perusal of the complaint and charge sheet averments, it makes it clear that the complainant is the legally wedded wife of the petitioner.
It is an admitted fact that after marriage, the complainant was residing with her in-laws in her matrimonial house.
She became pregnant.

She was taken to NC: 2023:KHC-D:13115 hospital for routine check-up and several allegations have been made against the brother-in-law, father-in-law and mother-in- law in respect of termination of pregnancy and sexual assault etc.
However, no allegations made against the petitioner herein.
Even though the provisions under the POCSO Act is made out against the petitioner, Section 375(2)(n) of IPC not attracted against him.
Having considered the said aspect, the petitioner being a husband of the complainant, is entitled for bail.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition is allowed.
The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in Crime No.06/2023 of Sirigiri Police Station, on executing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One lakh only) with one surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the Trial Court,
subject to the following conditions:
a) The petitioner shall not threaten or tamper the prosecution witnesses nor hamper the proceedings of the Court.
b) The petitioner shall not leave the jurisdiction of the Court till disposal of the case.
